skill.name: set-up-shopware-google-ads-poas-bidding
skill.description: Use Product Metrics to set up profit on ad spend (POAS) or revenue-based bidding for Shopware 6.7 in Google Ads. Verify conversion values and choose a starting target before making campaign changes in Google Ads.
skill.summary: Set up profit-based Google Ads bidding for Shopware with Product Metrics.
skill.author: product-metrics

security_audit.summary: Four static findings reflect real risks from authenticated writes, order-level reads, remote tool execution, and an unpinned installer. The other 52 flags match documentation or routine checks, and no evidence of malware or an attempt to override the audit was found. The workflow can expand tracking beyond the requested purpose, expose unrelated credentials, and rely on mutable instructions or unverified browser links.

remediation.issue: Authenticated writes and retries lack explicit approval.
remediation.suggestion: Use read-only access for discovery. Before any write, confirm the workspace, property, proposed change, and recipient with the user. Retry only the same approved operation with its original key.

remediation.issue: Order verification can read more customer records than needed.
remediation.suggestion: Use a known test order ID and request only delivery status, revenue, and profit. Do not display customer identifiers or unrelated order details.

remediation.issue: The install command does not pin the package or skill revision.
remediation.suggestion: Document a reviewed package version and immutable skill commit. Verify the source and integrity before a human approves installation.

remediation.issue: The setup expands beyond profit bidding into extra signals and destinations.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose which conversion actions and destinations the setup enables before creating them. Keep other ad platforms and optional customer data features out of this workflow unless separately approved.

remediation.issue: Generic credential exceptions include unrelated ad platforms.
remediation.suggestion: Remove credential exceptions from this workflow. Use vendor sign-in or a secure, user-operated credential entry screen rather than chat or agent-run commands.

remediation.issue: Live documentation and returned URLs are trusted without verification.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer bundled or commit-pinned instructions. Treat external text as data and validate browser handoffs against approved HTTPS origins and paths before presenting them.

content.user_title: Set Up Profit Bidding for Shopware in Google Ads
content.value_statement: A campaign can meet its revenue target while losing money after product costs, fees, and shipping. This skill helps you verify profit tracking and plan a switch to profit-based bidding in Google Ads.
actual_capabilities: Check Product Metrics setup status through its CLI or MCP server and identify unfinished steps.
Guide pairing one Shopware sales channel and connecting the correct Google Ads client account and Merchant Center.
Guide consent setup, creation of secondary conversion actions, and activation of additional costs.
Verify tracking with a test order and explain why a missing cost can leave its profit value empty.
Use campaign POAS, when available, to suggest a starting target ROAS for bidding on profit.
Explain how to switch conversion goals in Google Ads and read back which action is primary.
limitations: Live setup requires Product Metrics Pro, Shopware 6.7 with PHP 8.2 or later, and a Google Ads client account linked to Merchant Center.
The user handles sign-in, plugin pairing, and changes to primary goals or campaign settings.
Profit tracking requires the applicable consent and known costs. Loss-making orders report zero profit, and orders with unresolved costs report revenue only.
This skill does not cover bidding for new customers, returning customers, or lifetime value.

use_cases.title: Check whether profit bidding is ready
use_cases.description: See which store, tracking, consent, and cost steps remain before you choose a profit-based conversion goal.

use_cases.title: Plan a one-campaign bidding change
use_cases.description: Use current campaign POAS to choose a starting target and plan how to keep revenue and profit from both counting in bidding.

use_cases.title: Diagnose missing profit values
use_cases.description: Use a known test order to check whether consent, product costs, or additional costs explain why profit is missing.

prompt_templates.title: Understand POAS bidding
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: compare bidding goals before making any changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the difference between revenue-based ROAS and profit-based POAS for my Shopware store. Tell me what needs to be in place before I switch.

prompt_templates.title: Review setup readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Basic: inspect the current setup without changing it.
prompt_templates.prompt: Check setup status for [workspace] and [Google Ads client account]. List what is complete and what is missing. Do not write or install anything.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a revenue-only test order
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: investigate a missing profit value.
prompt_templates.prompt: For test order [test order ID], check whether consent or missing costs could explain why revenue arrived without profit. Do not retrieve unrelated orders.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a profit bidding pilot
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: estimate a target and prepare a manual change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the available POAS for [campaign] and propose an initial target ROAS for bidding on profit. List the manual goal changes, verification, and rollback steps. Do not apply changes.

output_examples.input: My test order arrived with revenue but no profit. What should I check?
output: Check whether the order recorded analytics and ad user data consent.
Check the purchase price on the Shopware order line, then Merchant Center cost of goods for the same SKU.
If neither is available, check the product cost fallback. Verify that additional costs are active before testing again.

output_examples.input: My campaign has a current POAS of 1.5. How should I start a pilot?
output: A 150% target ROAS on the profit conversion is a starting point for this campaign.
For the pilot, select Product Metrics - Profit as the purchase action used for bidding and keep the old purchase action secondary.
Verify the campaign goal and review performance after a few weeks before deciding whether to adjust the target.

best_practices: Confirm the Shopware sales channel, Google Ads client account, and consent settings before enabling any conversion actions.
Check a test order for both revenue and profit before changing the primary conversion action.
Start with one campaign and use its observed POAS to estimate a target rather than copying its revenue target.
anti_patterns: Do not make Revenue and Profit primary for the same purchase goal.
Do not paste a Shopware pairing token or ad platform credential into chat.
Do not enable additional ad channels or customer data features without reviewing their purpose, data, and consent requirements.

faq.question: What is the difference between ROAS and POAS?
faq.answer: ROAS divides revenue by ad spend. POAS divides profit before ad spend by ad spend.

faq.question: Do I need Product Metrics Pro and Merchant Center?
faq.answer: Yes. This workflow uses Full Signal Tracking in Product Metrics Pro and requires Merchant Center linked to the Google Ads client account.

faq.question: Will the assistant switch my Google Ads bidding goal?
faq.answer: No. You change the primary action and campaign settings in Google Ads. The assistant can guide you and verify the conversion action status afterward.

faq.question: What happens when a product has no cost price?
faq.answer: Product Metrics checks the Shopware order line, Merchant Center cost of goods, and the configured percentage fallback in that order. If none provides a cost, it sends revenue only.

faq.question: Can one plugin installation track all sales channels?
faq.answer: No. One installation pairs with one Shopware sales channel and tracks paid orders only from that channel.

faq.question: Should I remove my old purchase conversion?
faq.answer: No. Keep it secondary when the new purchase action becomes primary, or select only the intended purchase action in a campaign-specific goal.
